findings.en_sentence: The known fossil material consists of a fragmentary skeleton that lacks the skull.
findings.es_sentence: El material fósil conocido consta de un esqueleto fragmentario que carece del cráneo.
findings.problem: Says all known material lacks the skull, but two sentences later the paratypes include skull fragments; the source applies 'lacking the skull' only to the holotype specimen.
findings.correct: The holotype is a fragmentary skeleton without the skull; skull fragments are known only from paratype material.

findings.en_sentence: He originally classified Kaijiangosaurus within the family Megalosauridae.
findings.es_sentence: Originalmente clasificó a Kaijiangosaurus dentro de la familia Megalosauridae.
findings.problem: 'He' (ES: subject left out) refers to someone the page never introduces: the describer He Xinlu (1984).
findings.correct: He Xinlu, who described it in 1984, originally placed Kaijiangosaurus in Megalosauridae. / Su descriptor, He Xinlu (1984), lo clasificó originalmente en Megalosauridae.

findings.en_sentence: Kaijiangosaurus possessed megalosaurid-type teeth with few serrations near the tip.
findings.es_sentence: Kaijiangosaurus poseía dientes del tipo megalosaurídeo con pocas sierras cerca de la punta.
findings.problem: Drops 'leading edge': the source says only the front (mesial) edge has a few serrations near the tip, not the tooth as a whole.
findings.correct: Its teeth are of the megalosaurid type; the front edge has only a few serrations, near the tip. / ...el borde anterior solo tiene unos pocos dentículos, cerca de la punta.

findings.en_sentence: Some researchers suggest Kaijiangosaurus may be an ancestor of carnosaurs based on its cervical vertebrae showing both carnosaurian and primitive traits.
findings.es_sentence: Algunos investigadores sugieren que Kaijiangosaurus podría ser un ancestro de los carnosauros, basándose en que sus vértebras cervicales muestran tanto rasgos carnosauros como primitivos.
findings.problem: Comes from an old eswiki claim (which also wrongly says it is known from a single vertebra); 'ancestor of carnosaurs' is an outdated, overstated idea, presented in present tense, and it is not paleobiology. Modern work treats it only as an indeterminate basal tetanuran/averostran.
findings.correct: Its describer noted that its neck vertebrae mix carnosaur-like and more primitive traits; early on this was taken to suggest it was close to the origin of carnosaurs (in the past tense, in classification).

findings.en_sentence: Due to fragmentary remains, it is uncertain whether Kaijiangosaurus is a specific type of tetanuran theropod, though it may be a primitive carnosaur.
findings.problem: Garbled: the source says it is unclear what kind of tetanuran it is, not 'whether it is a specific type'.
findings.correct: Because the remains are fragmentary, it is unclear what kind of tetanuran it is, although it may be a primitive carnosaur.

findings.en_sentence: Kaijiangosaurus lived during the Middle Jurassic, approximately 165 to 161 million years ago (Bathonian and Callovian stages), in what is now Asia.
findings.problem: Leaving this out, the Spanish page has no time_and_habitat section, and it also lacks the F011 debate sentence; both are on the EN page.
findings.correct: Add the Spanish equivalents: 'Vivió en el Jurásico Medio (Bathoniense–Calloviense)...' and 'Por lo fragmentario de los restos, no está claro qué tipo de tetanuro es, aunque podría ser un carnosaurio primitivo.'
findings.checked_in: texts es.json vs en.json, built pages

findings.en_sentence: Kaijiangosaurus lived during the Middle Jurassic, approximately 165 to 161 million years ago (Bathonian and Callovian stages), in what is now Asia.
findings.problem: 165–161 Ma covers only the Callovian (Bathonian is about 168.2–165.3 Ma), and it does not match the page's own header (168.2–161.5 Ma).
findings.correct: ...about 168 to 161 million years ago (Bathonian–Callovian), in the Lower Shaximiao Formation of Sichuan, China.
findings.checked_in: F013 (eswiki intro), ICS chart, built page header

findings.en_sentence: Paratypes include fragmentary skull remains, nine teeth, pectoral girdle elements, a forelimb, and a hindlimb.
findings.es_sentence: Los paratipos comprenden restos fragmentarios del cráneo, nueve dientes, elementos del cinturón pectoral, un miembro anterior y un miembro posterior.
findings.problem: 'Cinturón pectoral' is a calque of 'pectoral girdle'; the anatomical term in Spanish is 'cintura escapular/pectoral'.

findings.en_sentence: The holotype proper includes the intercentrum of the atlas and the third through ninth cervical vertebrae.
findings.es_sentence: El holotipo propiamente dicho incluye el intercentrum del atlas y las vértebras cervicales tercera a novena.
findings.problem: Leaves the English/Latin 'intercentrum' untranslated; the Spanish term is 'intercentro'.
findings.correct: ...el intercentro del atlas y las vértebras cervicales tercera a novena.

findings.en_sentence: Kaijiangosaurus possessed megalosaurid-type teeth with few serrations near the tip.
findings.es_sentence: Kaijiangosaurus poseía dientes del tipo megalosaurídeo con pocas sierras cerca de la punta.
findings.problem: 'Sierras' is not the term used for tooth serrations; Spanish paleontology uses 'dentículos' (or 'aserraciones').
findings.correct: ...con pocos dentículos cerca de la punta.
